does: Flattens a dough with a rolling pin into an even sheet of the thickness the dish asks for, whether thin enough to see through, for a filled pastry, or thick enough to stay soft, for a flat bread.
how: Rest the dough first, or it will spring back. Shape it into a flat round or square before the pin touches it.
Dust the surface and the pin lightly with flour, so that the dough slides and does not stick.
Roll from the middle outwards in one steady push, lift and give the dough a quarter turn, and roll again.
Turn the dough over now and then and dust again only where it sticks.
Stop when the sheet is even from edge to edge. Let it rest and spring back before it is cut or filled.

cues.text: The sheet is even, with no thick middle or thin rim and no tears.
The dough slides freely on the surface when it is nudged.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling a tense dough that keeps shrinking back.
mistakes.fix: Cover it and let it rest, then roll again.

mistakes.mistake: Dusting with too much flour, which dries the dough and leaves white streaks.
mistakes.fix: Use only as much as it takes to stop it sticking, and brush off the extra.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling over the edges, which leaves them thin and the middle thick.
mistakes.fix: Roll from the middle outwards and stop short of the edge.

comes_after.why: A dough has to be smooth and rested before it rolls out evenly without tearing.
